text:
maria: Heads-up: warm-node pool in ap-southeast1c is flapping. ~30 pods pending with FailedAttachVolume and nodes showing NotReady during init. Anyone oncall?

noah: I'm here. Any kernel logs or 'ss' output?

maria: Pulled `ss -s` on a healthy warm node vs a bad one: healthy shows ~1.2k TCP sockets, bad node: TCP: inuse: 42000 orphan: 0 tw: 38000 alloc: 64 mem: 1

ash: 38k TIME_WAITs -> ephemeral port exhaustion. Does our nvme attach helper open short-lived connections?

maria: The nvme attach helper talks to the local attach service over unix domain socket, but our metrics exporter and gpu-health-checks open TCP probes to the metrics aggregator in the same AZ. I see many sockets stuck in TIME_WAIT with local ephemeral ports in the 32k-60k range.

vik: Also ran `sudo conntrack -L | wc -l` on one node: 64000 entries. Kernel nf_conntrack_max is 65536. We're at the ceiling. That explains netlink ops timing out during attach.

infra-bot: alert: ap-southeast1c warmpool socket/conntrack saturation — affected nodes warm-node-aps3-{06..10}.

noah: Immediate plan: 1) bump nf_conntrack_max to 200k on affected nodes, 2) rotate metrics exporter on each node to close stale sockets, 3) restart kubelet and attach helper. Do rolling 1 node at a time.

maria: Agreed. I'll run an SSM command to set `sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=200000` and restart services. Starting with warm-node-aps3-06.

ash: Can we also temporarily change scheduler affinity so warmpool nodes don't get new warm-start jobs? We should avoid hitting more nodes while we heal.

routing-bot: Soft routing change applied by noah: avoid ap-southeast1c for new warm starts for 45m; prefer: [us-west2, eu-west1].

maria: After the sysctl + restart on 06, `ss -s` shows TIME_WAIT down to 1200 and conntrack at 2k. Pod attach succeeds and the node becomes Ready. Rolling to 07 next.

vik: Root cause hypothesis: our node metrics exporter doesn't reuse keepalive or mishandles TLS renegotiation which leaves sockets in TIME_WAIT. It also spawns short-lived probe workers on error without reusing connections.

noah: Longer term: 1) fix exporter to reuse keepalive and close properly (ash will take PR), 2) add conntrack/ephemeral socket alarms to warmpool ASG (maria), 3) add exponential backoff and jitter to attach init so a transient netlink hang doesn't block many pods at once (infra runbook change).

ash: I'll open a branch for exporter fixes and include unit tests that simulate TLS renegotiation and confirm sockets are closed.

maria: Also, action item: add a kernel tunable to set net.ipv4.tcp_tw_recycle off/adjust TIME_WAIT reuse and increase local_port_range to avoid ephemeral exhaustion. We should document tradeoffs with TCP reuse.

vik: Note on cost: routing ~90 warm-start jobs to eu-west1/us-west2 for 40m added an estimated $900 of cross-region egress and spot churn. Finance pinged.

noah: After 45m, routing-bot reverted routing. Warmpool healthy. Closing incident once exporter PR and alarms are in place.

infra-bot: incident resolved by maria at 11:07 UTC — warmnode pool stable.

maria: Runbook entry created: Confluence: /warmpool/socket-saturation-runbook (internal). I pushed the SSM snippets and the one-liners we used.

ash: Will post PR link when ready. Thanks all.
